method.tool: scratchpad/tools/coverage_search.py --whole-words --regex, eight term sets (search/C6/terms.txt); S1-S3 re-run in the foreground because the first background runs were empty
method.record_check: independent front-matter grep (recgrep.py -> recgrep.json); records read via show-*.txt dumps and showc.py
method.verification: verify.py: quote text normalised and searched in the vendored file named by the source record; three records checked by hand (see verified[].detail)
method.layers: RENDERED = a record speaks to the sub-question (R* = partial, or an honest_limit/guard only); LOADED = a vendored file mapped to the world holds a passage read in context; IDENTIFIED = registered, unvendored source record; OTHER = outside the repo; NOTHING. Drafts are marked; lpc is entirely draft with no package.

sub_questions.label: Who led, how chosen, what the titles meant, bishops or not, could a congregation remove one
The pope and Rome; Peter and 'on this rock'
Councils and creeds; who decided disputes; did ordinary believers have a say
Tradition and scripture; apostolic succession; the only true church; is there a church today that is yours
Heresy: who decided, what happened to heretics
Leaders who failed, got rich, or abused; distrust of leaders; lonely leaders and divided congregations

S1.note: Titles and the bishop's role are covered (episkopos; Clement's three ranks) and one bishop-against-teacher break is told twice. Nothing says how a bishop was chosen or whether a congregation could remove one. Jerome Ep. 146 (presbyters named their bishop at Alexandria down to Heraclas) is vendored under hal's map, not alx's.

source_hits.snippet: Dionysius of Rome pressing the test on his namesake of Alexandria, who did not decline it (Robertson)

S2.note: No alx record names Rome, pope or Peter. The vendored hits are about Rome and Alexandria in the 250s and the 340s and are read in context.

S3.note: Strongest council answer in the cluster for a pre-Nicene world: teachers, then bishop, then council; denies the council voted. Ordinary believers appear only as village presbyters and teachers at Arsinoe. The creed question gets the rule of faith (not a written creed); the Nicene creed is a source record with no quote.

S4.note: Tradition, rule of faith, 'catholic' as wholeness and the honest stop on any church today are all rendered. Apostolic succession of bishops is not claimed by any record; Origen's 'orderly succession' is of teaching.

S5.note: Boundaries with Gnostic and Arian rivals are said to be real and enforced, and the world owns the force used after Nicaea. No quote shows a heretic being dealt with.

S6.note: Deacons appear only as a heavenly rank in Clement. Nothing on what they did, on deaconesses or on married clergy.

S7.note: Both sides of the Constantinian change, with Athanasius's exiles as proof and a verified line from the Festal Index. Does not say whether the emperor dictated belief at Nicaea.

S8.note: The record leaves the bishop-against-teacher wound visible and has a divided-villages story (Arsinoe) for R-40. Nothing on a lonely leader or on abuse.

S1.note: Sees, village bishops, simony letter, synod deposition: 'not one clean process' is said outright. No record has a congregation removing a bishop; synods and emperors do it.

S3.note: The creed as written-down worship, not a vote; the Homoian reversal shows that emperors and synods decided too. Ordinary believers: only through the font and the doxology.

S4.note: The best tradition-beside-scripture answer in the fleet, with the honest 'no signed receipt back to the apostles'. Apostolic succession of bishops is not rendered.

S1.note: One of three worlds with a demonstration on F3-I-05, and the fullest on how a bishop was made against his will; the capture claim is held Contested.

S2.note: 'Pope' as a title of honour, the Apostolic See as Rome and not a supremacy. 'On this rock' is not rendered.

S3.note: Two houses, two answers: Vincent trusts ancient councils, Martin never entered a synod again. Laity: nothing.

S4.note: Vincent's test is the best statement of tradition in the fleet. Apostolic succession is explicitly not claimed (not_for in apostolic-authority).

S5.note: Heretics cast out by bishops and never put to the sword; Martin against the Priscillian trial.
